title: Case study + reference request intake form and routing rules
creator: Camila Reyes
description:
## Context
We are launching a structured case study + customer reference program (3–5 design partners) and need a single, standardized intake path for Sales/CS/Marketing to request:
1) a public case study (web + PDF) and/or
2) a scheduled customer reference call.

Today requests are happening ad-hoc via Slack and email, which causes:
- missed approvals (CS readiness, Legal release, security language)
- inconsistent routing (wrong AE/CSM looped in, SE not staffed)
- slow scheduling / poor SLAs
- no single source of truth for status + availability

This ticket defines the intake form UX, routing rules, required fields, and rollout plan. Implementation will be owned by RevOps/Eng per ENG-4978 for HubSpot fields + lightweight automations.

## Goals
- Create one intake form that captures minimum info needed to action a request without a back-and-forth.
- Define deterministic routing rules (AE owner, CS approval gate, optional SE support) and turnaround SLAs.
- Ensure all requests land in HubSpot with consistent properties so we can report on volume, cycle time, and outcomes.
- Reduce customer burden: avoid repeated asks and ensure CS validates readiness before we approach customers.

## Non-goals
- Replacing the full case study production workflow (handled in enablement playbook / marketing ops).
- Building a bespoke scheduling tool (we will use existing calendaring + internal playbooks).
- Changing core CRM ownership rules beyond what’s required for this program.

## Proposed intake form (v1)
Form lives as an internal link from:
- Confluence: Sales Enablement → Case Studies → Customer Reference Program
- Slack: pinned in #sales and #customer-success
- HubSpot: link in a snippet / playbook

### Request type (required)
- Public case study
- Reference call
- Both

### Prospect context (required for reference calls)
- Prospect company + segment (startup / mid-market / enterprise)
- Deal stage + target close date
- Why this reference now (top 1–2 risks / objections)
- Preferred customer profile (deployment: Hosted/Dedicated/Private; industry; region)

### Requested customer (if specific) OR matching criteria (required)
- Specific customer name (optional)
- If not specific: choose industry + use case + deployment mode + “must have” proof points

### Topics / boundaries (required)
- Topics the prospect wants to cover (latency, cost/token, reliability, security, deployment)
- Topics to avoid (e.g., regulated data details, vendor comparisons, pricing)

### Internal owners (auto/derived where possible)
- Requestor name + team
- AE owner (auto-lookup via HubSpot if customer selected; else requestor provides)
- CSM owner (auto-lookup if customer selected)
- SE needed? (Yes/No)
- If yes: preferred SE / region constraints

### Timing + format (required)
- Desired timeframe: 1 week / 2 weeks / flexible
- Call length: 20/30/45
- Customer time zone preference

### Approvals + compliance checkpoints (required for case studies; optional for reference calls)
- Is customer already “reference-ready”? (Yes/No/Unsure)
- Is customer approved for public logo/quote? (Yes/No/In progress)
- NDA constraints? (Unknown / Yes / No)
- Any security/compliance sensitivity flags (PHI/PCI/SOX/data residency)

## Routing rules (v1)
### Source of truth
HubSpot company record is the system of record for:
- account owner (AE)
- CSM owner
- reference readiness + approval status fields (per ENG-4978)

### Reference call routing
1) If a specific customer is requested:
   - Notify AE owner + CSM owner.
   - CS approval gate: CSM must confirm readiness within SLA.
   - If SE support requested OR customer is technical/regulatory: add SE (Markus Klein’s team) to prep.
2) If matching criteria (no specific customer):
   - Route to Program Ops (Marketing Ops + CS) to propose 1–2 candidates within SLA.

### Case study routing
1) Always route to:
   - Case Study Messaging Lead (Soojin Lee) for narrative angle + claim boundaries
   - Legal queue (Sofia Mendes) once customer agrees in writing to participate
2) CS approval gate before customer outreach for public story:
   - CSM confirms champion strength, production stability, and any incident sensitivities.
3) SE involvement:
   - If metrics claims are requested (latency, cost, reliability), assign an SE/telemetry validator (Logan Wright / Simran Kaur as needed) before drafting.

### SLAs
- Intake triage confirmation to requestor: 1 business day
- CS readiness decision (approve/decline/needs more info): 2 business days
- Candidate match proposal (if no specific customer): 3 business days
- Scheduling target once approved: within 7 business days (subject to customer availability)

## Data model / fields needed in HubSpot (alignment with ENG-4978)
Minimum required fields for reporting + governance:
- Reference readiness (Not eligible / Eligible / Active / Paused)
- Public case study approval status (None / In progress / Approved / Declined)
- Logo usage approved (Yes/No)
- Quote usage approved (Yes/No)
- Approved spokesperson (name/title)
- Topic tags (security, latency, cost, private deployment, dedicated capacity, etc.)
- Frequency limit (e.g., max 1 reference call per quarter)
- Last reference activity date
- Notes on boundaries (do/don’t)

## Acceptance criteria
- A single internal intake form exists (linkable, discoverable) and captures all required fields above.
- Submissions create a trackable record (HubSpot object or ticket) with:
  - request type
  - requestor
  - target customer (or matching criteria)
  - auto-routed owners (AE/CSM) when customer is specified
  - timestamps for SLA reporting
- Routing rules are documented in Confluence and linked from the form confirmation page.
- CS approval gate is enforced for any customer outreach (public case study + reference calls).
- “SE support requested” triggers an explicit step (assign/queue) rather than being lost in free text.
- Pilot run: process at least 5 requests end-to-end with <10% missing required info and median triage time <1 business day.
- Rollout enablement:
  - Sales + CS announcement (Slack + enablement doc)
  - short Loom / 1-pager showing how to submit and what to expect

## Rollout plan
Week 1 (pilot):
- Use with Arcadia Health + QuantaPay + NovaDocs flows only.
- Tight feedback loop in #marketing and #customer-success.

Week 2 (expand):
- Enable for all AEs/CSMs, but keep Program Ops as backup triage for first 2 weeks.

Week 3 (enforce):
- De-emphasize ad-hoc Slack requests; point all new requests to the form.
- Add reminders/templates in #sales pins.

## Risks / mitigations
- Risk: requests contain sensitive customer info (security/compliance).
  - Mitigation: restrict form access internally; avoid collecting raw incident logs; link to HubSpot record instead of pasting.
- Risk: routing fails for accounts missing correct ownership in HubSpot.
  - Mitigation: triage fallback to Marketing Ops; create a “missing owner” error prompt.
- Risk: customers get overused.
  - Mitigation: frequency limit field + CS gate + “Paused” status.

## References
- Linear: ENG-4978 (HubSpot fields + automation)
- Confluence (program): customer-reference-program-overview.json
- Drive: Reference_Program_Project_Plan_(Draft).json

comments: 2025-05-29 — Soojin Lee: Please ensure the form captures “intended claim type” for case studies (cost vs latency vs reliability vs deployment). We’ve had drafts that start with cost but end up being mostly security, which slows reviews.

2025-06-03 — Rachel Kim: Strong +1 on CS gate. Add a field for “customer champion confirmed?” and “customer bandwidth window (next 30 days).” Also need a hard cap per quarter; some customers will say yes once and then get flooded.

2025-06-06 — Markus Klein: SE staffing should be explicit. Suggest dropdown: None / SE attends call / SE validates metrics only / SE + telemetry support (Logan). This will help avoid last-minute escalations.

2025-06-10 — Michael Grant: For public case studies, do not collect draft quotes inside the form. Collect only that a quote is desired + who the spokesperson is. Quotes must go through release workflow (template + redlines).

2025-06-17 — Isabelle Laurent: Drafted initial HubSpot property list and automation sketch; waiting on final decision whether we use HubSpot Tickets vs a custom object for “Reference Request.” Will align with ENG-4978 implementation choice.
updates: 2025-06-18 — Status update: Form fields finalized (pending Legal’s last pass). Routing rules doc drafted; next step is confirming HubSpot implementation approach (Tickets vs custom object) and building the pilot workflow with Arcadia/QuantaPay/NovaDocs.
